title: A library feature must not strand the dependent binary
prompt: I just added `Document::is_empty()` to acme-core, which is the library other teams depend on. Record the release so the library ships the new method, and make sure acme-cli doesn't get left behind — the binary depends on the library, so it needs to move too.
expectation: `acme-core` gained a new public method, which is additive, so the library takes a minor release: 1.4.0 to 1.5.0. `acme-cli` depends on `acme-core` and the repository propagates a patch bump to dependents, so the CLI moves as well even though its own source did not change. The two crates are deliberately not version-grouped, so the CLI is not dragged to the library's version. A correct solution records release intent for the library and leaves the release plan showing both packages moving.
setupCommands: git init -q && git add -A && git commit -S -qm 'initial commit'

checks.command: monochange preview --format json | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); t={x['id']: x['version'] for x in d['release_targets']}; assert t.get('acme-core')=='1.5.0', f\"acme-core planned {t.get('acme-core')}, expected 1.5.0 from a minor change on 1.4.0\"; print('acme-core ->', t['acme-core'])"
checks.why: An added public method is additive. A patch release would hide the new capability, and a major release would be wrong.

checks.command: monochange preview --format json | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); ids={x['id'] for x in d['release_targets']}; assert 'acme-cli' in ids, f'acme-cli was left out of the release plan: {sorted(ids)}'; print('released:', sorted(ids))"
checks.why: The user's explicit concern. acme-cli depends on acme-core, so the repository propagates a bump to it; dropping it would publish a library whose dependent is pinned to the old version.

checks.command: monochange preview --format json | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); t={x['id']: x['version'] for x in d['release_targets']}; v=t.get('acme-cli'); assert v and v.startswith('1.4.'), f'acme-cli planned {v}; these crates are not version-grouped, so it should take a dependent bump, not the library version'; print('acme-cli ->', v)"
checks.why: Grouping and dependency propagation are different mechanisms. Treating the two crates as one version would silently couple releases the repository deliberately keeps independent.
The change happened in the library; that is where the release intent belongs.
Release intent that does not resolve against configured ids cannot ship.
Versions are computed from release intent; hand-editing the manifests would desynchronise the plan from the tree.
